mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when INDPRO rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when CPIAUCSL rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when HOUST falls for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the GDP price index (GDPC1) over three consecutive quarters signals economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when GDPC1 rises for three consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).
